about.heading: Processable amorphous coordination networks
paragraphs: Wenlong Xue works on the chemistry and processing of hybrid glass frameworks, MOF glasses, and amorphous proton conductors. The research combines coordination-network design with mechanochemistry, melt processing, thin-film preparation, and structure-property analysis.

Current work at KU Leuven focuses on directly synthesised amorphous networks, local structure and transport mechanisms, and device-oriented routes for integrating proton-conducting hybrid glasses into energy and separation technologies.

research.heading: From ordered frameworks to functional hybrid glasses
research.intro: Research is organised around the design, transformation, and application of coordination networks that bridge crystalline MOFs, liquids, glasses, and device-processable films.

items.title: Direct synthesis of amorphous conductors
items.text: Asymmetric and flexible linkers are used to redirect oxide-to-framework reactions from crystallisation to glass formation, enabling bulk amorphous networks without relying only on melt-quenching.

items.title: Transport mechanism and local structure
items.text: Synchrotron PDF, XAS, solid-state NMR, impedance spectroscopy, and molecular modelling are combined to reveal how local coordination order supports long-range proton transport.

items.title: Device-oriented processing
items.text: Thin-film growth, lithographic patterning, and membrane-electrode integration are developed to evaluate hybrid glasses under realistic energy-device conditions.

platforms.heading: A modular platform for materials discovery and device validation
platforms.intro: The website is prepared as a personal academic site, while the content structure already supports expansion into a research-group website with group members, open positions, facilities, teaching, and collaborations.

items.title: Micro-Nano Device Platform
items.text: Patterned MOF-glass thin films, interdigitated electrode arrays, and chip-level proton-transport screening.

items.title: Fuel-Cell and Electrolyser Platform
items.text: Membrane-electrode integration, gas-barrier and conductivity evaluation, and long-term durability at 150-250 deg C.

items.title: Materials Library
items.text: Directly synthesised amorphous networks, hybrid glass membranes, modifier chemistry, and composition-structure-property mapping.

contact.heading: Collaborations and enquiries
contact.text: Research discussions, synchrotron proposals, student enquiries, and collaborative projects in hybrid glasses, MOF processing, and proton-conducting materials are welcome.
